title: Parallels Desktop Flaw Lets Unprivileged Mac Users Gain Root Access
content_md: A critical local privilege-escalation vulnerability in Parallels Desktop for Mac could allow an unprivileged local user to execute attacker-controlled code with root privileges, placing developer workstations and shared macOS systems at risk. Tracked as CVE-2026-90894 and dubbed “ParaShells” by JFrog researchers, the flaw affects the privileged prl_disp_service daemon, which Parallels Desktop uses to manage virtual machines, networking components , and appliance installations. JFrog confirmed exploitation against Parallels Desktop 26.4.0 build 57513 on Apple Silicon systems. Parallels addressed the issue in Desktop 27.0.0. Parallels Desktop Flaw The issue is significant because exploitation does not require administrator rights, a signed Parallels client, or an active virtual machine. An attacker only needs code execution under a low-privileged local macOS account on a system where Parallels Desktop and its root-level dispatcher service are installed. Yuval Moravchick found that the service exposes the Unix socket /var/run/prl_disp_service.socket with world-writable permissions, allowing any local process to connect. The service’s PrlSrv_LoginLocal authentication path reportedly accepts requests based on local peer credentials rather than verifying that the connecting client is signed by Parallels.
